title: The Cauchy–Binet formula
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $m,n\ge0$ integers, $A=(a_{ij})$ an $m\times n$ matrix and $B=(b_{jk})$ an $n\times m$ matrix with entries in $R$ [def-weil-matrix], and $AB$ their product, the $m\times m$ matrix with entries $(AB)_{ik}=\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij}b_{jk}$. For a subset $S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ with $|S|=m$, let $A^{S}$ be the $m\times m$ submatrix [def-weil-submatrix] of $A$ formed by the columns with indices in $S$ and $B_S$ the $m\times m$ submatrix of $B$ formed by the rows with indices in $S$, both taken in increasing order of the indices. Then, with $\det$ the determinant of a square matrix [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], $$\det(AB)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\},\ |S|=m}\det(A^{S})\det(B_S)$$ in $R$. (For $n<m$ the sum is empty and $\det(AB)=0$; for $m=0$ both sides are $1$.)

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00AR (section-rings-basic), list item Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet, line 282), stated there without proof as a basic fact

proof.text: (Expansion.) Write $[m]=\{1,\dots,m\}$. By the definition of the determinant [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] and of the product, $\det(AB)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_m}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{k=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n a_{\sigma(k)j}b_{jk}$. Expanding the product of the $m$ sums by distributivity, $\prod_{k=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n x_{k,j}=\sum_{f:[m]\to[n]}\prod_{k=1}^m x_{k,f(k)}$ (one term for each choice of an index $f(k)$ in the $k$-th factor), so, exchanging the two finite sums and using commutativity of $R$, $$\det(AB)=\sum_{f:[m]\to[n]}\Big(\prod_{k=1}^m b_{f(k)k}\Big)\sum_{\sigma\in S_m}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{k=1}^m a_{\sigma(k)f(k)}=\sum_{f:[m]\to[n]}\Big(\prod_{k=1}^m b_{f(k)k}\Big)\det(A_f),$$ where $A_f$ is the $m\times m$ matrix [def-weil-matrix] with $(A_f)_{ik}=a_{i,f(k)}$ (column $k$ of $A_f$ is column $f(k)$ of $A$), the last equality being the definition of $\det(A_f)$.

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00AR (section-rings-basic), list item Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet, line 282), stated there without proof

proof.text: (Non-injective $f$ contribute $0$.) If $f:[m]\to[n]$ is not injective, there are $k\ne l$ with $f(k)=f(l)$; then $(A_f)_{ik}=a_{i,f(k)}=a_{i,f(l)}=(A_f)_{il}$ for all $i$, so columns $k$ and $l$ of $A_f$ are equal and $\det(A_f)=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-det-repeated-column-zero]. Hence in step 1 the sum may be restricted to the injective maps $f:[m]\to[n]$.

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00AR (section-rings-basic), list item Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet, line 282), stated there without proof

proof.text: (Injective maps by image and permutation.) For $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|=m$ write $S=\{s_1<\dots<s_m\}$. The map $(S,\tau)\mapsto f$, $f(k)=s_{\tau(k)}$, from pairs of such a subset $S$ and a permutation $\tau\in S_m$ to injective maps $[m]\to[n]$ is a bijection: $f$ is injective as a composite of injective maps, with image $S$; conversely an injective $f$ has an image $S=f([m])$ with $|S|=m$, and $\tau(k)$ is then forced to be the unique $t$ with $s_t=f(k)$, which defines a permutation $\tau$ of $[m]$ because $f:[m]\to S$ and $t\mapsto s_t$, $[m]\to S$, are bijections. (If $n<m$ there is no such $S$ and no injective $f$.)

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00AR (section-rings-basic), list item Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet, line 282), stated there without proof

proof.text: (The term of $f=s\circ\tau$.) Let $S=\{s_1<\dots<s_m\}$ and $f(k)=s_{\tau(k)}$ as in step 3. By the definition of the submatrices [def-weil-submatrix] taken in increasing order, $(A^S)_{it}=a_{i,s_t}$ and $(B_S)_{tk}=b_{s_t,k}$ for $1\le i,t,k\le m$. Hence $(A_f)_{ik}=a_{i,s_{\tau(k)}}=(A^S)_{i,\tau(k)}$: $A_f$ is $A^S$ with its columns permuted by $\tau$, so $\det(A_f)=\operatorname{sgn}(\tau)\det(A^S)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-det-column-permutation]. And $\prod_k b_{f(k)k}=\prod_k b_{s_{\tau(k)},k}=\prod_k(B_S)_{\tau(k),k}$.

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00AR (section-rings-basic), list item Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet, line 282), stated there without proof

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By steps 1–4, $$\det(AB)=\sum_{|S|=m}\sum_{\tau\in S_m}\Big(\prod_{k=1}^m(B_S)_{\tau(k),k}\Big)\operatorname{sgn}(\tau)\det(A^S)=\sum_{|S|=m}\det(A^S)\sum_{\tau\in S_m}\operatorname{sgn}(\tau)\prod_{k=1}^m(B_S)_{\tau(k),k}=\sum_{|S|=m}\det(A^S)\det(B_S),$$ the last equality being the definition of $\det(B_S)$ [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. For $n<m$ both the sum over injective $f$ and the sum over $S$ are empty and $\det(AB)=0$; for $m=0$ the only $f$ is the empty map, the only $S$ is $\emptyset$, and both sides are $1$.

split_report.summary: Mathlib has no Cauchy-Binet formula (LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle and grep re-run on 2026-10-10 in addition to the citer's searches; the nearest is ExteriorPower/Basis.lean ιMultiDual_apply_ιMulti, which gives it only by a multi-line argument), so the item is split. Stacks 0F0K (tag checked in tags/tags: algebra-item-cauchy-binet, algebra.tex line 282) states it without proof; the proof is written by the agent in five steps: expansion of det(AB) by the Leibniz formula and distributivity into a sum over maps f:[m]->[n] of (prod_k b_{f(k)k}) det(A_f) (elementary from the new definition node); non-injective f vanish (repeated column, new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-det-repeated-column-zero = Matrix.det_zero_of_column_eq); injective f correspond bijectively to pairs (S, tau) (elementary); det(A_{s o tau}) = sgn(tau) det(A^S) (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-det-column-permutation = Matrix.det_permute'); recombination into det(A^S) det(B_S) by the Leibniz formula (elementary). No DAG node defined the determinant of a square matrix (def-weil-endomorphism-determinant is the determinant of an endomorphism of a free module), so the new Mathlib leaf def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant (Matrix.det with Matrix.det_apply, same index convention prod_k M_{sigma(k),k}) is created and added to stmt_deps; the statement now also defines the product AB inline, otherwise unchanged. The citer lem-weil-pbc-matrix-left-inverse-minors step 4 applies the statement to (B, A) with B m x n, A n x m, which matches the indexing (columns of the first factor, rows of the second).

lean.statement: theorem cauchy_binet {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (m n : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) R) (B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) R) : let minors : R := ∑ S : {S : Finset (Fin n) // S.card = m}, (A.submatrix id (S.val.orderEmbOfFin S.property)).det * (B.submatrix (S.val.orderEmbOfFin S.property) id).det (A * B).det = minors ∧ (n < m → minors = 0 ∧ (A * B).det = 0) ∧ (m = 0 → (A * B).det = 1 ∧ minors = 1)

reviewed_lean.note: CommRing R (Stacks ring); m n : ℕ unrestricted; A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n), B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m); AB = rectangular A * B; S over {S : Finset (Fin n) // card = m} once each; increasing order via orderEmbOfFin shared by A^S columns and B_S rows via Matrix.submatrix; Matrix.det; main equality + both parenthetical cases as conjuncts; no Mathlib Cauchy-Binet (grep binet in 3 Mathlib checkouts: only CrossProduct/GoldenRatio)
